masthead.headline: Drive it before you read about it.
masthead.lede: The prototype below is the real thing, packed into this page and running in a sandbox. It is disposable: it exists to settle two questions about the merge interaction, and it will not become the implementation.

meta.label: Lifespan
meta.value: Until the merge plan is approved

sections.label: Drive it
sections.title: Merge the two cursor threads and watch what happens.

blocks.text: Press Merge on the first thread. Two things are worth watching: what happens to the count, and what the hint underneath changes to. Both are the subject of the questions further down.

blocks.title: Feedback queue — merge interaction
blocks.alt: A feedback queue of four threads. The first two are about the same cursor bug; the first carries a Merge 2 alike button. Pressing it folds the second thread away, drops the open count from four to three, and replaces the hint with a line saying folded threads are kept rather than deleted.

blocks.title: It cannot see this page
blocks.text: The prototype runs its own script — that is what makes it drivable — but it is denied access to this document, its storage, and every answer you type below. It behaves like itself while being unable to read anything around it.

sections.label: For contrast
sections.title: What the same queue looks like now.

blocks.title: Today's queue, for comparison
blocks.alt: The current console: a table of rows with status pills and no grouping, so duplicate threads appear as unrelated rows.
blocks.caption: Duplicates appear as ordinary, unrelated rows. Nothing on this screen says that two of them are the same complaint.

pins.text: These two rows are the same report. Nothing distinguishes that pair from any other adjacent pair, which is the problem the prototype is testing a fix for.

sections.label: What it settles
sections.title: The two things the prototype exists to answer.

blocks.label: Folded threads
blocks.ask: When threads merge, what should happen to the folded ones on screen?
blocks.recommendation: Collapse them under the survivor. Hiding them entirely is what the prototype does and it reads as deletion — three of four testers asked whether the thread was gone, which is exactly the doubt the merge feature cannot afford.

choices.summary: The folded threads stay visible as a count the reader can open.
pros: Unmerge is discoverable from where the merge happened
cons: A second state to design and to test at narrow widths

choices.value: Hide entirely, as the prototype does
cons: Unmerge has to live somewhere the reader has no reason to look

choices.summary: Nothing moves; folded threads dim and lose their actions.
cons: The queue does not get shorter, which is the point of merging

blocks.label: What you noticed
blocks.ask: Which of these did you notice while driving it?

options.summary: The open-thread count is the primary feedback that something happened.
The line about folded threads being kept is the only reassurance on screen.

options.value: The merge button became a label
options.summary: It stays visible as 'Merged 2' rather than disappearing.

options.value: I could not tell where the second thread went
options.summary: The failure mode this prototype was built to expose.

blocks.label: At phone width
blocks.ask: Switch the prototype to Phone and merge again. Does anything read differently?
blocks.placeholder: Particularly whether the hint is still visible when the merge happens.
